name: Video Chess (Atari 2600)
description: Probably the first digital chess game that you can play at home, now with the advantage to not have to wait 10 hours per move!

name: The Chessmaster (NES)
description: The most succesfull and recognizable chess game from the 80' and 90'

name: Battle Chess (NES)
description: It's cool and all, it gave a bit of personality to chess, still, it's pretty weak.

name: Sega Chess (Master System)
description: Sega first and only attempt at creating a chess game, it's pretty strong.

name: The Chessmaster (Genesis)
description: Sega decided to not develop any more games and let Chessmaster do the work, though they nerfed him a little, probably because of the fact that you needed internet to get this game in the first place.

name: The Chessmaster (SNES)
description: You wouldn't believe it! Another Chessmaster, third and last time, also this is the strongest of them all.

name: Sargon Chess (CD-i)
description: In my opinion the coolest one, even for the fact that Sargon commented on the game, the only downside is that the console itself was $799

name: Chess.com
description: The most famous chess website, you probably have an account, don't lie.

name: Chessbase.com
description: You probably never heard of it but surprisingly enough it's the strongest bot.

name: ShredderChess.com
description: Built in 1993, it has beaten many computer competitions.

name: Cardgames.io
description: Even though it is a card games based website, it has a chess engine, it's pretty good.

name: Myself
description: I suck at this game, you can probably beat me easily
